questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement scalable, policy-driven security in multi-tenant clusters, with clear tests.

## Key Concepts
- Admission controllers (Kyverno/OPA)
- NetworkPolicy default-deny per namespace
- PodSecurityContext: readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities.drop
- Privileged container restrictions and CI checks

## Code Example
```javascript
# Minimal Kyverno policy (YAML shown as JS block for readability)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: enforce-basic-security
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-psp
    match:
      any:
        - resources:
            kinds: [Namespace, Pod]
    mutate:
      patch: |-
        {"spec": {"securityContext": {"readOnlyRootFilesystem": true, "allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}}}
```
```javascript
# Failing manifest (privileged container)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
```
```javascript
# Passing manifest (no privileged, readOnlyRootFilesystem)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities:
        drop: ["ALL"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the policy locally and in CI across multiple namespaces?
- How would you handle exceptions for legacy workloads?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests practical, auditable governance for multi-team clusters beyond image/security gates.

Key Concepts

- Namespace governance with ResourceQuota and LimitRange
- Namespace-scoped RBAC and ServiceAccounts
- Lightweight CI gates using kubectl/yq
- Local validation vs CI parity

Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get resourcequota >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing ResourceQuota in $ns"; exit 1; }
  kubectl -n "$ns" get limitrange >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing LimitRange in $ns"; exit 1; }
  for dep in $(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {/end}'); do
    sa=$(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy "$dep" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}')
    if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "Deployment $dep in $ns uses default SA"; exit 1; fi
    kubectl -n "$ns" get rolebinding | grep -q "$sa" || { echo "Missing RBAC for $sa in $ns"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

Failing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: rq
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.memory: 16Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: lr
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "4"
      memory: 8Gi
    min:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a-view
  namespace: team-a
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: sa-team-a
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
```

Verification

- Locally: run the gate script against your cluster context and verify it fails/passes as expected; inspect output for missing quota/limitrange or RBAC gaps.
- CI: run the same script in a workflow step; ensure failing manifests fail the build and passing manifests pass.

Why This Is Asked

- Evaluates ability to translate security requirements into enforceable runtime and CI gates

Key Concepts
- Kyverno, Pod Security Standards, Resource limits, CI gates, Drift detection

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must define a secure securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop all capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: "true"
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
  - name: require-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must specify resource limits and requests"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This task tests practical CI gating for container hygiene: linting with Hadolint and enforcing image tagging discipline across manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Hadolint integration in GitHub Actions
- YAML parsing to inspect image tags
- Regular expressions for pinning (no latest, no -dev) and clear failure messages
- Practical debugging of lint vs. policy failures

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-docker-k8s.yml
name: CI Gate: Dockerfile lint + tag pin
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ '**' ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3
        with:
          dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
      - name: Check pinned image tags
        run: |
          set -e
          if grep -RIn 'image:.*:.*(latest|dev.*)' manifests || true; then
            echo 'Unpinned image tag detected' ; exit 1;
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this gate to many repos?
- How would you extend checks for other tag policies (sha256 digests)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of resource isolation and guardrails in multi-tenant clusters, plus practical policy tooling.

## Key Concepts

- ResourceQuota
- LimitRange
- Pod resource requests/limits
- Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-resource-requests-limits
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod","Deployment","StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must define cpu/memory requests and limits"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  requests:
                    cpu: "+"
                    memory: "+"
                  limits:
                    cpu: "+"
                    memory: "+"
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests API compatibility in a real-world microservices stack, a must-have for stable multi-service ecosystems. Uses consumer-driven contracts to decouple teams and catch breaking changes early.

## Key Concepts
- Pact/OpenAPI contract testing
- Provider verification against a catalog
- PR gating and contract versioning
- Central contract repository and workflow integration

## Code Example
```yaml
name: Pact Verification
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      - run: npm ci && npm run test:contracts
      - run: npx pact-verifier contracts/consumer/provider/pacts/*.json --provider-base-url http://provider-service:8080
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you evolve contracts when a breaking change is required?
- How do you manage contract catalogs across many services and teams?
